lines.trans: You see, we are an ideal and harmonious couple.
We love animals very much and take care of them.
In our good apartment it is always warm and peaceful.
Hector will be able to walk in the beautiful park every day.
And sleep on the soft couch by the bed.
The owner is very glad about our kind words.
She sees how much we suit each other.
Careful, Max, this is just our clever game.
The main thing is that the dog finally found its home.
I am sincerely happy to take this good dog.
Let's go quickly, Hector is waiting for us by the door.
Now our life will become much better together.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.
I'm listening right by my ear.
The car is parked near the house.

examples.text: Возле дома Аникеева ходили два подозрительных человека.
examples.trans: Near Anikeev's house two suspicious people were walking.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: neuter главное, used as a noun
neuter главное, used as a noun

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

гулять.gloss: to walk, to go for a walk

meanings.en: to walk, to stroll, to be outside
meanings.note: гулять с собакой = to walk the dog

examples.trans: A girl walks a little dog there.
Let's go for a walk in the park.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'door' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The door is behind the wardrobe.
Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'sofa, couch' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is sitting on the sofa.
I will reach the sofa myself.

meanings.note: in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!
There's a new building on Simashko Street.

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Наш коллектив маленький, но очень дружный.
examples.trans: Our collective is small, but very friendly.

examples.text: Телевидение покажет сюжет про вашу дружную семью.
examples.trans: Television will show a story about your united family.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

examples.text: Я добрый человек, я люблю животных.
examples.trans: I am a kind person, I love animals.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

заботиться.gloss: to care for; to look after

examples.text: Мне поручили заботиться о вас, Виктория.
examples.trans: I was assigned to take care of you, Viktoriya.

examples.text: Мы очень любим животных и заботимся о них.
examples.trans: We love animals very much and take care of them.

examples.text: Виктория просто заботится о дисциплине зала.
examples.trans: Victoria simply cares about the dining room discipline.

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement
забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'game, play' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это отличная игра! Хочешь с нами поиграть? Бери карты.
examples.trans: This is a great game! Want to play with us? Take the cards.

examples.text: Мы создадим идеальную команду для работы.
examples.trans: We will create an ideal team for work.

examples.text: Сегодня стояла идеальная погода для прогулки.
examples.trans: Today there was ideal weather for a walk.
For ideal order in the universe.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кренне').

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я вам искренне сочувствую.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I sincerely sympathize with you.

examples.text: Я вам искренне сочувствую, но мне пора работать.
examples.trans: I sincerely feel for you, but it is time for me to work.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: also a flat number in an address

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, handsome').

examples.trans: They have a very beautiful house.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'bed' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

examples.text: Мясо должно стать мягким и сочным.
examples.trans: The meat must become tender and juicy.

examples.text: У тебя очень милые мягкие кудри.
examples.trans: You have very sweet, soft curls.
But here the metal is too soft.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'конец').

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.en: much, far, a lot (before a comparative)
meanings.note: намного хуже = much worse; намного лучше = much better

examples.trans: In prison it will be much worse.

examples.text: Но я же вижу, как тебе плохо. В тюрьме будет намного хуже, поверь мне.
examples.trans: But I can see how bad things are for you. In prison it will be much worse, believe me.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pair, couple, match' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: match (in a relationship: я не пара вам = I'm no match for you)

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you.
They are a very handsome couple.

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам. Вы красавец, а я старая.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you. You're a handsome man, and I'm old.

examples.text: Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Grab the little dog in the park and run.
We are walking in the old park.
We are walking in the park.

подходить.gloss: to approach, to come up; to suit

meanings.note: очередь подходит = one's turn is coming up
это мне подходит = that suits me

examples.trans: Let's go, our turn in the queue is coming up.
The train is approaching the station.

examples.text: Я к печке подхожу. А он маячит перед глазами!
examples.trans: I walk up to the stove. And it dangles right before my eyes!
Can I go and have a look?

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dog, hound' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: To give boots to vicious dogs.

examples.text: Сначала мы отдадим твои сапоги злым псам.
examples.trans: First we will give your boots to the vicious dogs.

meanings.note: short form only: рад, рада, радо, рады; no long-form cases

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?
The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.en: to be able to, to manage to

examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.
Will you be able to come tomorrow morning?

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

meanings.note: grammatically feminine even for a male dog
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.
The film has a happy ending.

examples.text: Ты сейчас один против всех. Счастливого конца не будет.
examples.trans: Right now you're alone against everyone. There won't be a happy ending.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cunning, sly').

examples.trans: Be careful, he is very cunning.

хозяйка.gloss: landlady, hostess, mistress of the house

meanings.en: landlady, female owner, mistress of the house
meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'landlady, hostess, mistress of the house' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Right, hand over the money, landlady.

examples.text: Хозяйка квартиры живёт на первом этаже.
examples.trans: The landlady of the flat lives on the ground floor.
My wicked landlady kicked me out.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
